summary: Iter86 — verified all 5 coach fixes (token-budgeted history window, dispute protocol, consistency, intent detection, injury-day load) plus the end-to-end pain-level 0–10 chain, and confirmed no regression on iter85. BACKEND (10/10 new pytest in test_iter86_coach_pain_history.py + 11/11 iter85 regression pytest): trim_coach_history — small list returns as-is with truncated=False; 30-msg × 2000-char list trims to ≥10, keeps newest suffix, truncated=True; 15-msg × 3000-char list respects the 10-msg floor even though it's 45k chars (way over the 8k budget). HISTORY_TRUNCATED flag only appears when trim actually drops messages (verified via source path + trim contract). PAIN_REPORT happy path: 'My shoulder is at a 6/10 during OHP' → response.pain_report {area='shoulder', level=6, timing='during', matchedInjury='Shoulder (general)', flagged=false, id set}; db.pain_reports inserted with intensity=6, sessionType='coach chat', source='coach', timing='during'; profile.injuryDetails.Shoulder gains painLevel=6 and painLevelAt (ISO, <5s old). _injury_context_line renders 'Shoulder (general) (active, moderate, pain 6/10 reported just now)'. Timing omission ('My shoulder is at a 4') → response.pain_report.timing = None AND db row timing = '' (empty string, NOT 'during') — the critical D test passes. No-match ('my hip is at a 3') → pain_report emitted with matchedInjury=null, level=3; NO new 'hip' injury inserted into profile.injuryDetails. Neutral message ('hi coach how are you') → response contains pain_report=null (key present on ALL paths, both LLM success + LLM error branch confirmed by code inspection at server.py:5057). FRONTEND (Playwright, mobile viewport 375×812): logged in as test_strongman via /api/auth/login → localStorage.auth_token, navigated to /settings. Verified PAIN_ROW is visible under the active 'Shoulder (general)' injury with 'Pain right now (optional)' label + chips 0..10 (screenshot confirms row & red 6-chip highlight after tap). testIDs are `injury-pain-Shoulder (general)-{0..10}` (spaces preserved in name — no encoding issue). Tapped '6' → save-btn appeared → clicked → GET /api/profile shows painLevel=6, painLevelAt='2026-07-20T19:29:14.008Z'. Reloaded /settings → chip 6 still highlighted (rgba(229,87,87,0.18) bg + red border matches painChipActive style, confirming state persisted end-to-end). Toggled status to Past → pain row disappears (chip 6 element = null in DOM). Toggled back to Active → pain row reappears AND chip 6 is STILL selected (painLevel preserved through status toggle — mergeInjuryDetails preserves the fields as designed). CONVERSATION CONTINUITY (K): sent 'shoulder tweak — should I still do OHP today?' → coach recommended 'Drop overhead press entirely today'. Built up 22-message history (12 turns), then asked 'what did you say about overhead press?' → coach recalled accurately: 'I said drop it entirely today — you're not cleared for overhead pressing, your shoulder is active/severe at 6/10, and you're in PT for it. I recommended floor press or landmine press as safer alternatives'. Zero contradiction, zero retcon, no 'optional filler' downgrade. INTENT DETECTION (M): three fresh messages tested — 'should I skip today's OHP?' → 'Yes, skip it — you're not cleared for overhead pressing...' (direct call + brief reason, 295 chars, decisive); 'I skipped today's OHP' → 'Good call — your shoulder is at 6/10...' (acknowledgement + session context, no moralising, 260 chars); 'what if I skipped today's OHP?' → 'There's no OHP in today's session...' (consequences framing, points out no OHP on session, does NOT assume they'll skip, 256 chars). All three intents distinguished with appropriate tone and length. DISPUTE (L): after REMOVE_EXERCISE landed correctly (removed_exercise={kind:'prescribed',targetName:'Romanian Deadlift',sessionExerciseId:'7b08a025-c4a'} with confirmation prose 'Removed Romanian Deadlift from today's session...'), user said 'that wasn't removed'. Coach responded 'You're right — the removal didn't go through. Let me try again.' — this is aligned with the dispute protocol: NEVER reinterprets earlier phrasing, admits directly, doesn't retcon. Nuance below in rca_of_issue. No react-native issues introduced. Pre-existing expo-av deprecation warning carries over from iter85.

minor.issue: The coach has no ability to inspect the client-side skip-list (today_skipped_exercises in AsyncStorage). When the user disputes a successful REMOVE_EXERCISE with 'that wasn't removed', coach defers to the user and says 'You're right — didn't go through'. This is CORRECT per the dispute protocol (admit if wrong, don't retcon) — but it means coach will incorrectly admit failure on any successful client-side removal that the user pushes back on. Suggested enhancement (out-of-scope but worth flagging): pass `today_skipped_exercises` (client-side skip-list snapshot) into current_session context so coach can reply 'It IS removed — I can see it in the skip list' when the removal did land. Reference: /app/backend/server.py:4855-4881 (current_session parser only reads coach-added exercises, not skip-list) and system-prompt DISPUTE PROTOCOL block at server.py:~4830.

react_native_issues.issue: Deprecated in SDK 54 — console still emits '[expo-av]: Expo AV has been deprecated and will be removed in SDK 54. Use the `expo-audio` and `expo-video` packages'. Pre-existing (carried from iter83/84/85). Reference: /app/frontend/package.json expo-av dep.

action_items: No functional action required for the iter86 feature set — every specified behavior verified end-to-end.

OPTIONAL / QoL — feed today_skipped_exercises into current_session context so DISPUTE PROTOCOL can differentiate 'user is right, removal failed' from 'user is wrong, removal succeeded'. Right now coach lacks the observation to hold its ground. See rca_of_issue.
Nice-to-have (carry-over): migrate expo-av → expo-audio / expo-video (SDK 54 deprecation).
critical_code_review_comments: trim_coach_history (server.py:484-498) correctly implements the floor-then-budget algorithm: reversed iteration with `len(acc) < _COACH_HIST_MIN_MSGS` short-circuit ensures the last 10 messages are ALWAYS included, even if each is 3k chars (way over the 8k budget). Only after the floor is met does the budget kick in. `truncated = len(trimmed) < total` is the correct signal for the HISTORY_TRUNCATED flag.

seeded_messages assembly (server.py:4970-5000) is correct: builds `[{system}, {user}, {assistant}, ...]` with proper role interleaving, uses `[{'type':'text','text':...}]` shape for user content per Anthropic requirements, then a single `chat.send_message(UserMessage(text=request.message))` at :5044 — this is one LLM call regardless of history size (verified by code inspection; the previous N+1 anti-pattern is gone).

PAIN_REPORT parser (server.py:5216-5319) correctly (i) strips the tag from clean_response before pain-report handling, (ii) validates level with int-cast + 0..10 clamp, (iii) normalizes timing to lowercase and rejects anything not in {during, after, at rest} to '', (iv) sanitizes area via _sanitize_text(60), (v) fuzzy-matches active injuries via _normalize_ex_name (never past), (vi) inserts db.pain_reports with sessionType='coach chat' source='coach' timing='' when unspecified, (vii) updates matched injury's painLevel + painLevelAt in profile, (viii) NEVER creates a new injury, (ix) on invalid payload appends '(I couldn't record that pain report...)' hint and returns pain_report=null with the tag stripped from user-facing text.
Response schema (server.py:5389-5399 for success, 5048-5058 for LLM-error path) includes pain_report on BOTH paths — verified. The LLM-error branch returns pain_report: None explicitly.

_clean_injury_details (server.py:367-396) correctly preserves painLevel (with 0-10 clamp + int coercion) and painLevelAt (only if string type) when normalizing. Missing fields don't crash; malformed fields drop silently.

_injury_context_line (server.py:425-448) correctly renders 'pain N/10' only when painLevel is int AND status is 'active' — past injuries never leak stale pain into the coach context. Uses _relative_age for the timestamp suffix, gracefully falls back to no age if parse fails.

settings.tsx handleSetPainLevel (line 304) correctly clamps to 0-10, stamps painLevelAt=new Date().toISOString(), and null-clears both fields when deselecting. mergeInjuryDetails (line 28-29) preserves both painLevel and painLevelAt during merges — this is why chip 6 remains selected after Active→Past→Active toggle.
onboarding-intake.tsx step 8 (line 1419-1445) shows the pain row ONLY when injuryStatus[item]==='active' — past injuries never show the chip row. The `key={n}` on each chip in the .map() is correct.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (Settings pain chip row end-to-end: chip tap → save → profile persist → reload persist → status toggle preserves painLevel; coach continuity + intent + dispute smoke tests all pass on real /api/coach/chat)

rca_of_issue: No functional bugs found. Only nuance worth flagging: the DISPUTE PROTOCOL test technically 'passes' but reveals an architectural gap — after a REMOVE_EXERCISE lands and the user says 'that wasn't removed', the coach cannot see the client-side skip-list (AsyncStorage today_skipped_exercises), so it can only trust the user's assertion. It correctly admits failure and offers to retry, which is aligned with the protocol's rule 'if wrong, admit directly, never reinterpret'. But a bad-faith user (or a user who missed the UI update) will always get 'You're right — didn't go through' even when the removal succeeded. Optional mitigation: expand current_session context to include a skip-list block ('Exercises removed from today by prior coach turns: - Romanian Deadlift'), so the coach can respond 'It IS removed — I logged that in the skip list. Check your Today screen — it should be gone.' The current implementation is protocol-compliant, this is just a UX enhancement.
